claim_verdicts.evidence: RFC 9112 §2.1: "An HTTP/1.1 message consists of a start-line followed by a CRLF and a sequence of octets in a format similar to the Internet Message Format: zero or more header field lines, an empty line indicating the end of the header section, and an optional message body."
RFC 9112 §4: status-line = HTTP-version SP status-code SP [ reason-phrase ]; §2.1 covers headers, empty line, optional body.
RFC 9112 §2.2: "HTTP-message = start-line CRLF *( field-line CRLF ) CRLF [ message-body ]".

RFC 9112 §3.2: "A client MUST send a Host header field in all HTTP/1.1 request messages" and a server "MUST respond with a 400 (Bad Request) status code to any HTTP/1.1 request message that lacks a Host header field".
RFC 9112 §6.2: Content-Length "indicates the associated representation's data length as a decimal non-negative integer number of octets" and is used to determine message body length (§6.3).
RFC 9110 §15.3.5: "A 204 response is terminated by the end of the header section; it cannot contain content or trailers."
RFC 9110 §15.4.5: 304 indicates the client "already has a valid representation" and may reuse it.
RFC 9110 §9.3.1: "content received in a GET request has no generally defined semantics" — the lesson says "normally has none", which is supportable; keep wording.
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: a GET normally has no body
